## Natural history notes

A small sunfish characterized by its deep, rounded body, olive to golden sides, bluish markings on the head and body, and a dark opercular “ear” flap edged with pale or orange markings. In Florida, the Dollar Sunfish is found in slow-moving streams, swamps, sloughs, ponds, ditches, and vegetated backwaters, especially in shallow areas with aquatic plants, woody debris, and soft substrates. It feeds on small aquatic insects, crustaceans, worms, and other invertebrates, while males construct and guard shallow nests during the breeding season.
